culture_principles.name: Customer-backwards judgment
culture_principles.description: Strong Amazon-style reasoning starts from the customer problem, then connects the decision, mechanism, and result back to customer or business impact.

culture_principles.name: Ownership with measurable execution
culture_principles.description: Candidates should show personal accountability, concrete action, measurable results, and follow-through beyond narrow task assignment.

culture_principles.name: High-velocity decision discipline
culture_principles.description: The lens rewards fast but reasoned action, especially when a decision is reversible, while still requiring risk awareness and correction mechanisms.

culture_principles.name: Narrative clarity and structured reasoning
culture_principles.description: Amazon-style communication should frame the customer problem, evidence, alternatives, assumptions, risks, and recommendation clearly enough for challenge.

culture_principles.name: Raise standards through mechanisms
culture_principles.description: Senior answers should show durable mechanisms, operating standards, production thinking, and team-level improvement rather than only heroic effort.

culture_principles.name: Trust, safety, and consent as impact boundaries
culture_principles.description: Growth, productivity, and speed should not be credited as strong impact if they create unresolved safety, transparency, consent, or customer-trust risks.

hiring_signals.signal: Uses STAR-like structure with specific situation, personal action, trade-offs, and quantified result.
Connects technical, product, analytics, or operations work to customer and business outcomes.
Explains decision reversibility, risk, speed, and correction mechanisms.
For SDE and senior SDE roles, combines coding or system design depth with scale, production ownership, and operational consequences.
For BIE and analytics roles, defines metrics clearly, validates data, communicates uncertainty, and converts analysis into a decision.

For non-SDE technical roles, adapt the Amazon lens to the role evidence: Applied Science should test scientific/ML reasoning, Data Center should test safe operational troubleshooting, and Developer Advocate should test technical communication.
Acknowledges trust, safety, consent, and transparency risks when optimizing growth, speed, or productivity.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Generic claims of teamwork or leadership without individual action, mechanism, or measurable result.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Amazon hiring guidance emphasizes detailed examples, personal contribution, and data-backed impact.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Treating Amazon preparation as coding-only or culture-only.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Candidate accounts and official materials point to both role capability and Leadership Principle evidence.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Optimizing for internal convenience, vanity metrics, or speed without customer problem clarity.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Customer-backwards reasoning and Day 1 decision culture require customer impact and disciplined judgment.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Using Bias for Action to justify ignoring safety, consent, compliance, transparency, or trust.
anti_signals.risk_reason: External risk evidence shows these are material boundaries for credible customer and operational impact.

anti_signals.anti_signal: For senior roles, giving only task execution detail without scale, ambiguity, operating mechanism, or post-launch ownership.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Senior candidate voice and Day 1 operating sources emphasize ownership, scale, mechanisms, and high-quality decisions.

interview_patterns.pattern: Behavioral answers should be probed for STAR structure, personal action, quantified result, and Leadership Principle fit.
Interview loops use multiple interviewers and should be modeled as multi-signal evidence collection rather than one global impression.
SDE practice should include coding/problem solving plus follow-ups on trade-offs, scale, maintainability, and production impact.
Senior SDE practice should include system design, customer experience under failure, operational metrics, and post-launch ownership.
BIE practice should include SQL or analytical reasoning plus metric definition, data validation, stakeholder communication, and business decision impact.
Applied Science practice should test scientific framing, model or NLP reasoning, experimental design, evaluation quality, and ownership of research-to-impact trade-offs.
Data Center and operations-adjacent technical practice should probe safe troubleshooting, escalation judgment, root cause analysis, and operational reliability.
Product, program, and business roles should include customer-backwards cases, narrative reasoning, trade-offs, and decision reversibility.

honest_limits: This is a public-source draft lens and does not represent an official Amazon hiring standard.
Medium-derived candidate voice is summarized and lower-confidence until URL/provenance review is complete.
Private materials authorized by the project owner are included only as distilled aggregate patterns, not as raw article text or copied questions.
Role, level, country, interviewer, and year can materially change interview process and emphasis.
This v0.1 lens has static validation cases but is not approved for production screening until live answer backtesting and reviewer approval are complete.
Legal and regulatory sources are used as risk context and should not be overstated as a complete view of Amazon culture.
This v0.2 lens has structured evidence records and an evidence audit, but is still not approved for production screening.
Public source URLs and private-material provenance must be reviewed before v1.0 approval.
